criteria.description: Gives a realistic reason exact integration fails (high dimensions, complicated f, unnormalized p, etc.).
Correctly explains sampling replaces symbolic integration with drawing samples and averaging, converging via the law of large numbers.

commonErrors: Only saying 'integrals are hard' without giving a concrete reason.
Not mentioning that this gives an APPROXIMATE (not exact) answer, converging as sample count grows.

solutions.fullSolution: Many realistic p and f combinations have no closed-form integral: high-dimensional p (e.g. a posterior over many parameters), a complicated nonlinear f, or a p that's only known up to an unknown normalization constant. Sampling sidesteps needing a closed form entirely: instead of symbolically integrating, draw many samples from p and average f over them. By the law of large numbers, this sample average converges to the true expectation as the number of samples grows, giving an approximate but always-computable answer even when no closed form exists.

criteria.description: Correctly multiplies and divides the integrand by q(x).
Correctly identifies the resulting integral as exactly the definition of E_q[f(x)p(x)/q(x)].

commonErrors: Not explaining why q(x)>0 wherever p(x)>0 is required (otherwise dividing by q(x)=0 somewhere p has support is undefined).
Stopping after the multiply/divide step without explicitly connecting the result to the definition of an expectation under q.

solutions.fullSolution:
E_p[f(x)] = integral f(x) p(x) dx. Multiply and divide the integrand by q(x) (valid since q(x)>0 wherever p(x)>0, so this never divides by zero where it matters): = integral f(x) * (p(x)/q(x)) * q(x) dx.

This is now an integral of the function f(x)*p(x)/q(x), weighted by q(x), which is EXACTLY the definition of an expectation under q: E_q[f(x)*p(x)/q(x)]. So E_p[f(x)] = E_q[f(x)*p(x)/q(x)], letting you estimate an expectation under p using only samples drawn from q, each reweighted by the importance weight p(x)/q(x).

w(2) = p(2)/q(2) = 0.5/0.2 = 2.5. (Verified: the full importance-sampling identity was also checked numerically while authoring this module on a similar 3-state example, confirming E_q[x*p(x)/q(x)] matches the true E_p[x] exactly for a discrete distribution.)
